# Taylor Custom Horseshoeing

Farrier in Lexington, Kentucky

[(405) 555-3078](tel:(405) 555-3078) 1071 Saddle Ln, Lexington, KY40502

## About Taylor Custom Horseshoeing

Taylor Custom Horseshoeing operates out of Lexington, Kentucky, one of the most horse-dense regions in the world. The Bluegrass State is home to hundreds of thoroughbred farms, training facilities, and private stables, so local farriers here work with some genuinely demanding clients and high-value horses. Taylor specializes in draft horse shoeing and natural hoof care, two disciplines that require very different skill sets. If you're managing a working farm or a pleasure horse operation near Lexington, this is the kind of specialized service worth knowing about.

## Services

Draft Horse Shoeing

Corrective Trimming

Glue-On Shoes

Natural Hoof Care

## Specialties

Hunter/JumperWestern Performance

## Certifications

APF DiplomaAFA Certified Farrier

## Brands Used

Save EdgeBloom ForgeNC ToolLiberty

## Frequently Asked Questions

Does Taylor Custom Horseshoeing work with draft horses specifically?

Yes, draft horse shoeing is one of their listed services. Draft breeds like Clydesdales and Percherons have much larger hooves and require heavier stock shoes, so not every farrier is set up to handle them comfortably.

What are glue-on shoes and when are they a good choice?

Glue-on shoes attach to the hoof using adhesive rather than nails, making them ideal for horses with poor hoof wall quality, thin walls, or horses recovering from injuries. They're also used on foals and horses that can't tolerate the percussion of nailing.

How is natural hoof care different from a standard trim?

Natural hoof care follows specific principles aimed at mimicking the shape and function of a wild horse's hoof, promoting concavity and encouraging healthier hoof capsule development over time. It's often chosen by owners who prefer to keep their horses barefoot rather than shod.

How often should my horse's hooves be trimmed or reshod in Kentucky's climate?

Most horses do well on a 6 to 8 week cycle, though this can vary based on how fast your horse's hooves grow and how hard they're working. Kentucky's humid summers can accelerate growth and sometimes contribute to softening of the hoof wall.

What does corrective trimming actually involve?

Corrective trimming means the farrier is adjusting the hoof angle, heel height, or toe length beyond a standard maintenance trim to address a specific movement or conformation issue. It's often done in coordination with a vet when there's an underlying musculoskeletal concern.

Is Lexington a good place to find experienced farriers?

Lexington sits at the heart of Kentucky's horse country, which means farriers here typically work with a wide variety of breeds and disciplines. The concentration of thoroughbred farms and training centers in the region tends to push local farriers toward a higher baseline of experience.
